ghi: NHÁP lời mới N6 (chưa thu; giọng khuôn T3/T4: hiện tại, câu ngắn, trích nguyên văn trong ngoặc). Tổng ≤ 10 câu chạm tới, ≤ 2 000 ký tự.

cau.vi_tri: mở lạnh M00 (phương án A), trước L01
cau.en: September 1666. From an alehouse on this bank, a man watches the City burn.
cau.nguon: Pepys 2/9/1666 (pg4167.txt dòng 1193–1194: 'a little ale-house on the Bankside')

cau.en: “A most horrid malicious bloody flame,” he writes, “not like the fine flame of an ordinary fire.”
cau.nguon: Pepys 2/9/1666 (pg4167.txt dòng 1197–1198: 'a most horrid malicious bloody flame, not like the fine flame of an ordinary fire')

cau.vi_tri: shot mới H1-12x (P2, Old St Paul's trong giàn giáo), sau L24
cau.en: Six days before the fire, John Evelyn and Christopher Wren had surveyed its decay — and proposed crowning it with a dome.
cau.nguon: Evelyn 27/8/1666 (pg42081.txt dòng 916 'with Dr. Wren'; dòng 932 'build it with a noble cupola')

cau.vi_tri: M-d mới H1-06x (sà lan hoàng gia), sau L14
cau.en: That afternoon, the King and his brother James, Duke of York, take to the river in the royal barge, ordering houses pulled down “apace”.
cau.nguon: Pepys 2/9/1666 (pg4167.txt dòng 1168–1170: 'Met with the King and Duke of York in their barge ... Their order was only to pull down houses apace')

cau.en: In the last days of the fire, the King and the Duke work the fire-lines themselves — “even laboring in person,” Evelyn writes.
cau.nguon: Evelyn 6/9/1666 (pg42081.txt dòng 1061–1066: 'the vigilance and activity of the King and the Duke was, even laboring in person'); Pepys 3/9 (pg4167.txt dòng 1238–1240: 'did ride with his guard up and down the City')

cau.en: Portland stone is so hard to come by that the column takes six years.
cau.nguon: City of London, themonument.org.uk/history: 'It took six years to finish, partly due to the difficulty of obtaining enough Portland stone of the required dimensions'

cau.cu: The last stone of the lantern is set in 1708.
cau.en: The last stone of the lantern is set in 1708 — by Wren's son, Christopher.
cau.nguon: St Paul's 'Our timeline': 'In October 1708 ... the last stone was laid on the lantern ... performed by Wren's son Christopher'; Parentalia 1750

cau.cu: On London Bridge, the houses and shops are pulled down in 1758.
cau.en: On London Bridge, the houses and shops are pulled down from 1758.
cau.nguon: London Museum object 99769: 'When the houses were cleared in 1758-62'; BHO (Thornbury 1878): 'not removed till 1757–60'

cau.cu: Between 1864 and 1870, the Victoria Embankment pushes the north bank out into the Thames.
cau.en: Between 1864 and 1870, Joseph Bazalgette's Victoria Embankment pushes the north bank out into the Thames.
cau.nguon: BHO Old and New London vol. 3 (node 37832): 'commenced in February, 1864, and completed in July, 1870'; 'Sir Joseph W. Bazalgette'

cau.cu: Winston Churchill reportedly sends word that St Paul's must be saved at all costs.
cau.nguon: không tìm được văn bản sơ cấp/cơ quan: St Paul's 'Our timeline' 1940 không nhắc; Historic England 403; các nguồn còn lại thứ cấp, không dẫn tài liệu gốc
